info.title: FreightSight API
info.description: Landed cost allocation and container tracking for SMB importers. Pre-alpha.

get.description:
Is this API able to serve? Railway uses it as the deploy healthcheck.

Which is why a dead worker must not fail it: the day the worker crashes is the day you most
need to be able to deploy a fix. `worker_seen_at` is reported here for whoever is reading,
and `GET /healthz/worker` is the probe that actually fails on it.

The probe an external uptime service points at, separately from the API's own.

Nobody would otherwise know the worker had died: there is no exception to report, there is
no process, and every screen goes on showing the numbers it last computed while the alerts
that the product is sold on quietly stop being raised.

post.description:
Fill an empty organization with a demo dataset. Refuses once it holds any data.

`reference` is one shipment, two containers and the invoice of the sales demo; `history` is
twenty containers over the last six months, for the screens that draw a trend.

delete.description:
Take the demo dataset away: what it created, and what only existed because of it (a cost typed
on a demo container goes with the container). Real data tied to it is refused by name, never
deleted along: a line of the user's own order in a demo container, a cost from an invoice they
uploaded, a draft pushed to their ERP.

get.description:
What this deployment has switched on, in terms of what a customer can rely on: are alert
e-mails really sent, are containers tracked without typing, is the worker alive, were the backups
checked. An alert that is logged instead of sent looks, from every other screen, exactly like one
that was sent. States and codes only: never a key, never a variable name.

schema.title: Response List Suppliers Api V1 Suppliers Get
Response List Purchase Orders Api V1 Purchase Orders Get

get.description: The catalogue in SKU order. `q` matches the SKU or the description, accents and case ignored.

post.description:
Create the entry, or update the one that already has this SKU (then 200, not 201): a catalogue
is filled from files and from screens alike, and neither should have to ask first.

One entry per article already ordered, carrying the latest description, tariff heading, duty
rate, weight and volume any order gave it. Entries that exist are left exactly as they are.

delete.description: Order lines keep what they copied: deleting an entry moves no landed cost.

schema.title: Response List Rate Cards Api V1 Organization Rate Cards Get

delete.description: Deleting a card leaves the estimates it produced alone: they are costs now, not derivations.

post.description:
Fill in what this container is expected to cost, from the rate cards and the tariff rates.

One transaction, and never a second estimate for a cost type that already has one: running this
twice is a no-op, which is what makes it safe to offer as a button.

get.description:
Estimated against invoiced, for the invoices dated in one month.

Grouped by cost type and by purchase order, because those are the two questions: which charge
surprised us, and which order carries the surprise. The split by order is the engine's own
allocation of each invoice, not a proportion invented here.

Landed cost by supplier, route, month or charge, over the period the goods landed in.

The period is about arrival, not invoicing: a forwarder billing six weeks late must not move last
quarter's numbers.

What demurrage and detention cost, and what acting in time plausibly saved.

Paid is a fact. Avoided is an estimate that each line justifies in words, and that does not exist
at all without the organization's own daily rate: a made-up saving is the kind of figure that
destroys trust in every other number on the page.

`basis=arrival` counts what the boxes that arrived in the period cost, whenever it was invoiced —
the audit's reading, since detention is billed after the empty comes back.

The first screen in one call: the period (the last ninety days by default) against the same
number of days before it, and what is waiting for somebody today. Every figure is the one the
detailed report gives for the same dates.

The audit of a period: the margin a purchase-price pricing overstates, what is worth a claim
to the forwarders, what demurrage cost, the measured coefficient against the assumed one, and
how complete the figures are. One computation; every section's total is the platform's. A period
that ends before it starts, or outside the years 2000 to 2100, is refused with PERIOD_INVALID.

Before auditing a period: what would make the audit wrong — boxes with no date, no goods, no
freight, invoices not yet read, costs the engine could not place, one invoice recorded twice —
then what it will not be able to say. Counts, amounts and examples by id; the same computation and
the same rules as the audit. A period that makes no sense is refused with PERIOD_INVALID.

Every article that travelled in the period: quantity, FOB, landed cost, the weighted unit
cost, how the last arrival compares with the one before, and the margin when the catalogue holds
a selling price.

One article, one point per container that carried it, oldest first, each with the cost types
that made up its landed cost. The SKU is a parameter because a SKU may contain a slash.
How this SKU's landed unit cost moved, one point per day it was recomputed.

Every month a container arrived in, newest first: open months with today's figures, closed
months with the frozen ones and how far today's have moved from them.

post.description:
Freeze the landed cost of the containers that arrived this month, line by line. Nothing is
locked afterwards; the figure frozen here simply never moves again.

delete.description: Undo a close. The frozen figures are deleted; the audit log keeps what they were.

post.description:
The drift as it stands today has been booked as an adjustment in the open month: the closed
month stops asking for it. A cost that arrives later makes it ask again, for the difference.

schema.title: Response List Shipments Api V1 Shipments Get
Response List Containers Api V1 Containers Get

patch.description: Manual tracking: milestone, timestamps, free days. A tracking provider replaces this in Phase 2.

schema.title: Response Get Loads Api V1 Containers  Container Id  Loads Get

put.description: Replace the full list of loads for this container. Refuses to over-allocate a PO line.

schema.title: Response Replace Loads Api V1 Containers  Container Id  Loads Put

post.description:
Store the connection — after proving it works.

The test happens before anything is written: a saved connection that has never authenticated is
a promise the next sync will break, and the error the ERP gives is far more useful now, while
the person who typed the credentials is still looking at them.

delete.description: Forget the ERP. The orders already imported stay: they are ours now.

post.description:
Read the ERP now, in this request.

Deliberately synchronous: someone has just connected their Odoo and is watching this button.
The daily refresh is the job; this is the reassurance. `full=true` re-reads the whole history
instead of what has changed — the button for "this looks wrong, start again".

schema.title: Response List Sync Runs Api V1 Erp Sync Runs Get

get.description:
What we would write into the ERP for this container, and what stands in the way.

Writes nothing, on purpose: the person clicking should see the object before it exists.

post.description:
Create the landed cost in the ERP, in draft.

Never validated by us: validating posts accounting entries in someone else's books, and that
decision belongs to whoever owns them. Pushing the same costs twice returns the first push
rather than writing a second document.

get.description:
Every landed cost we have written for this container, newest first.

Forgotten ones included, and marked: they are the record of something that was in the customer's
books, and hiding them would make the audit trail a shorter story than what happened.

schema.title: Response List Pushes Api V1 Containers  Container Id  Erp Pushes Get

delete.description:
Forget a push whose document is gone from the ERP, so its costs can be pushed again.

Not a deletion: the row stays and says it was forgotten, by whom and why. It is the only record
that we once wrote into someone's accounts, and the audit log points at it.

get.description:
One row per load, and the same numbers as the on-screen report — because they are its numbers.

The export used to add the allocations up a second way and forgot what every other surface of the
product applies: import VAT is recoverable and does not belong in a landed cost. The file the
finance director reconciles against his trial balance was inflated by exactly the VAT he claims
back. It now reads `organization_report`, so the CSV and the container report cannot diverge
again, and the VAT stands in a column of its own.

The period is read against the arrival date, like the landed-cost report on screen; a cost that
never reached a container has no arrival date, so the trailing `UNALLOCATED` rows are filed under
their own date and say so in `period_basis`. Their amounts are what the sum of `allocated` is
missing: an export whose total is quietly short of the invoices is an export nobody can use.

One row per cost piece, over the period the pieces are *dated* in.

Which is not the period `landed-costs.csv` answers to — that one files a cost under the month its
goods landed. A freight invoice dated 28 August on a container arrived 4 September belongs to
August here and to September there, and the totals of the two files cannot match. That is a fact
about invoicing, not an error, so every row names the date its period was read against.

One row per purchase-order line, which is the level anything is decided at.

The period is read against the order date, like the orders list on screen — a third date again,
and again named on every row.

The stock valuation a closed month froze: one row per article, with the quantity, the purchase
price, the landed cost and the unit cost as they went into the accounts. 404 for an open month —
the point of this file is that it never changes.

What has moved since a month was closed, container by container: the adjustment to book in the
open month, with the costs behind it.

The invoices not yet received at the end of the month, per container and cost type: frozen at
the close for a closed month, today's view of that date for an open one (`period_status` says
which). It is the cut-off statement; it proposes no accounting entry.

The landed unit cost of every article, to update the cost price in the ERP or the stock sheet:
the quantity-weighted average of the month, or that of the last container that landed. A closed
month gives its frozen figures. Without `period`, everything that has landed so far.

A plain, well-titled CSV on purpose: article imports are configured on the software's side
(Sage, EBP, Odoo all map columns), and no vendor format is invented here.

The findings of a period's audit, one per line: what to claim, what to check, and on which
container and invoice — the list a buyer takes to the forwarder. A period that ends before it
starts, or outside the years 2000 to 2100, is refused with PERIOD_INVALID, as on the screen.

schema.title: Response List Costs Api V1 Costs Get

post.description:
Close an estimate no invoice will ever match — "the forwarder never billed the inspection".

The estimate stops being allocated but is not deleted: what was expected and never charged is
part of the story of the shipment, and deleting it would quietly change past landed costs.
Same report with per-cost-type method overrides, nothing persisted. Powers the UI live switch.

get.description: Every cost is either fully allocated (Σ allocations == amount_base) or reported as unallocated.

schema.title: Response List Imports Api V1 Imports Get

post.description:
Upload a CSV/XLSX. Returns detected columns and a suggested (or remembered) mapping.

Nothing is written yet.

get.description:
What each kind of file reads, in the order a quarter is loaded — the catalogue first, since it
lends its rates only to the order lines written after it — with the header each column carries
in either language. A template written with these headers maps itself.

schema.title: Response Import Kinds Api V1 Imports Kinds Get

delete.description:
Take a costs file back: every cost it wrote is deleted, and the estimates they had replaced
stand again. Refused by name once a cost is in the ERP (COSTS_PUSHED_TO_ERP) or in a closed month
(IMPORT_PERIOD_CLOSED, with its `months`); a file taken back once answers IMPORT_ALREADY_UNDONE.

post.description:
Dry run: the commit code path under a SAVEPOINT that is rolled back.

The report is exactly what commit would do. For containers, costs and products the job keeps what
the preview ran with — the mapping, and for costs the type of the rows no label types and the
types a person gave the labels it could not read — and the commit runs with exactly that.

Write the file. Containers, costs and products write exactly what the preview a person approved
showed, named by its `preview_key`: without one, 409 PREVIEW_REQUIRED; when another preview of the
file replaced it, or the books have moved since and the same file would now do something else,
nothing is written and 409 PREVIEW_CHANGED carries the new `report` and its `preview_key`.

Accept a file and open an invoice on it. Reading happens in a job; this answers immediately.

`default_container_id` is for an invoice dropped from a container's page: the lines on which
the reading finds no container or order of its own are proposed on that container, and say so.

The extraction job is deferred inside this transaction: if the upload rolls back, the job never
existed either.

schema.title: Response List Invoices Api V1 Invoices Get

patch.description:
Correct the header the reader took — the number, the forwarder, the date — before confirming.

Every guard against counting one invoice twice compares the number and the forwarder, and the
confirmation writes them on each cost: a date read as the number is a false « already recorded »
today and a missed double entry tomorrow. Only while the invoice is being reviewed; what a
confirmed invoice says is corrected by reopening it.

get.description:
The file itself, streamed by the API.

Never a storage URL: a document stays behind the same authentication and the same tenancy checks
as its metadata, wherever its bytes happen to live.

patch.description: Correct what was read, and accept the line or not. This is the human half of the loop.

post.description:
Add the charge the reading missed — the other half of « it does not add up ».

The arithmetic check is only worth printing if the screen it prints on can answer it: a line the
patterns dropped because its wording carried « TVA 20 % », or a charge on a second page nobody
read, otherwise sends the reviewer off to key a cost somewhere else, unlinked to the invoice it
came from and flagged as a duplicate on the next one.

Create the accepted lines as costs — all of them, or none of them.

One transaction: the costs, the invoice's new status and the recomputed allocations land
together. A line pointing at something that is not ours stops the whole confirmation.

Put an invoice back in review without re-uploading the file.

A rejected one only changes status. A confirmed one gives back what it wrote: the costs it
created are deleted in this same transaction and the audit entry names them, so the correction
the forwarder sent the next morning is made on the invoice it belongs to. Once those costs have
reached the customer's ERP the confirmation stops being ours to undo, and the service refuses.
Not our invoice, a duplicate, an error: it stays on file, it creates nothing.
Read the document again — after a fix on our side, or once a model key exists.

get.description: 1 `quote` = rate `base` on `on_date` (ECB reference, cached).

schema.title: Response List Alerts Api V1 Alerts Get

get.description: The number behind the bell, for clients that want it without the list.

History, newest first, paginated by cursor.

A cursor rather than an offset because the log grows while it is being read: with an offset, an
entry written between two pages shifts everything and something is silently skipped.

Containers, orders, articles, invoices, suppliers and shipments whose name or number matches.

Case, accents, spaces and punctuation are ignored ("mscu 482" finds MSCU4821990). The whole
reference comes before its beginning, which comes before a match in the middle. Fewer than two
characters is not a question yet: the answer is an empty list, not an error.

post.description:
Freeze this container's landed-cost report as it stands and return a link to it. The token is
in this answer and nowhere else: only its hash is kept.

Freeze the audit of a period as it stands and return a link to it: the document of the paid
offer, sent to somebody who has no account. The subject of the share is the organization itself.
With `redact_vendors`, forwarders, invoice numbers and suppliers are left out of the snapshot.

schema.title: Response Audit Shares Api V1 Reports Audit Shares Get
Response Container Shares Api V1 Containers  Container Id  Shares Get
Response Purchase Order Shares Api V1 Purchase Orders  Po Id  Shares Get

delete.description: The link stops working at once. The row stays: the history of what was sent, and when.

post.description:
No account, no organization: the token is the whole of the right, and what it opens is the
snapshot taken when the link was made. Unknown, expired and revoked are the same 404 — an answer
that told them apart would tell a stranger which tokens once existed.

The token travels in the body, never in the URL: a URL is what access logs, error reports and
proxies keep, and this one is a bearer credential.

get.description: The container's timeline, oldest first, estimates included.

schema.title: Response List Events Api V1 Containers  Container Id  Events Get

post.description:
Record a milestone by hand and re-derive the container from its whole history.

Entering the same milestone at the same instant twice is not an error and writes nothing new.

schema.title: Response Add Event Api V1 Containers  Container Id  Events Post
Response List Eta History Api V1 Containers  Container Id  Eta History Get

post.description:
Start tracking this container.

With a `provider_ref` the deployment is in webhook-only mode: the provider was subscribed
elsewhere (its dashboard, another account) and we only need to know how to route its deliveries.
Without one, the provider's API is called, which needs a key.

delete.description: Stop tracking. The events already collected stay: they are the container's history.

post.description:
Accept one tracking delivery.

Answers 401 when the signature does not check out or the delivery is too old, and 200 for
everything else — including a replay and a delivery we cannot route — because a provider retries
on anything else and there is nothing to gain from being retried.

AlertResponse.title: AlertResponse
AlertResponse.description:
`title` and `body` are English sentences kept for API clients and logs. A screen builds its
own sentence from `kind`, `payload` and `container_number` in the reader's language.

AuditFinding.title: AuditFinding
AuditFinding.description:
One measured fact about the period's invoices, never an accusation: the rule that produced it,
how sure it is, how much money it is about, and the objects behind it.

AuditHeadline.title: AuditHeadline
AuditHeadline.description: The first page. Each figure is the sum of its section: the screen adds nothing.

AuditPage.title: AuditPage
AuditPage.description: A page of history, newest first. `next_cursor` is null when there is nothing older.

AuditPreparation.title: AuditPreparation
AuditPreparation.description:
What to put right before auditing a period: only what was found, blocking first. Not part of the
audit, and never sent with it: a working list, not a result.

AuditReport.title: AuditReport
AuditReport.description:
Frozen into the snapshot of every audit sent by link, and validated again at each opening: once
a link exists, this changes only by adding fields that may be absent.

AuditRules.title: AuditRules
AuditRules.description:
The thresholds the audit was produced with, for the page that states its method. Amounts are in
the base currency. A copy sent by link keeps the rules it was computed under.

ConfidenceBand.title: ConfidenceBand
ConfidenceBand.description: How much of a second look a reading needs. `confidence` keeps the number as it is.

ContainerDetail.title: ContainerDetail
ContainerDetail.description: GET /containers/{id}: the container, and what the accounts hold of it.

CostClose.title: CostClose
CostClose.description: Closing an estimate no invoice will ever match.

fx_rate.title: Fx Rate
fx_rate.description: Manual override; otherwise ECB rate at cost_date

CostStatus.title: CostStatus
CostStatus.description:
A cost is either what someone expects to pay or what was actually invoiced.

The whole point of the distinction: a landed cost can be right on the day the container lands,
from estimates, and become exact as invoices arrive — with the gap between the two visible.

ErpConnectionCreate.title: ErpConnectionCreate
ErpConnectionCreate.description: Everything needed to reach an Odoo. The API key is sealed before it is stored.

ErpLandedCostPreview.title: ErpLandedCostPreview
ErpLandedCostPreview.description:
Exactly what would be created in the ERP, and everything standing in the way of it.

Nothing is written to produce this.

EstimateResponse.title: EstimateResponse
EstimateResponse.description: What applying the rate cards to a container produced, and what it did not.

ExtractorKind.title: ExtractorKind
ExtractorKind.description:
Who read the document, in words a finance director can be shown.

The extractor's own name — « regex », « llm » — is our plumbing and reaches a CFO's screen
through the API. The name stays, because that is what a support ticket needs; this is what the
front translates.

ImportCreditNote.title: ImportCreditNote
ImportCreditNote.description:
A negative line left out of the books — costs cannot be negative — and counted, never dropped in
silence: it may refund a charge the audit would otherwise claim. Amounts as the file wrote them:
negative.

ImportFieldInfo.title: ImportFieldInfo
ImportFieldInfo.description:
A column an import reads, and the header the templates and the application's own exports give
it in each language: a file written with either maps itself.

ImportMoney.title: ImportMoney
ImportMoney.description: What a costs file puts in the books, in the organization's currency: the money first.

ImportReport.title: ImportReport
ImportReport.description:
What a preview found or a commit did. The counters of the other kinds are absent, not zero;
a preview or commit refused as a whole says so in `code` and `error`.

ImportRowIssue.title: ImportRowIssue
ImportRowIssue.description:
One thing to say about one row: `code` and `params` are what the screen words; `message` is
the English fallback.

ImportUnknownLabel.title: ImportUnknownLabel
ImportUnknownLabel.description: A label no rule can type, with what hangs on it: a person gives it a type (`label_types`).

InvoiceConfirmRequest.title: InvoiceConfirmRequest
InvoiceConfirmRequest.description:
Confirm again after looking at what a check found. Each flag answers one check only, and both
may be sent together; what was overruled is written into the confirmation's notes.

InvoiceLineCreate.title: InvoiceLineCreate
InvoiceLineCreate.description:
The charge the arithmetic says is missing, added by the person who is looking at the PDF.

It arrives like every other proposal — unaccepted, at zero confidence — so the rule holds: what
becomes a cost is what someone ticked, whoever typed it.

InvoiceLineUpdate.title: InvoiceLineUpdate
InvoiceLineUpdate.description: A correction made by a person. Everything is optional; nothing is inferred.

InvoiceStatus.title: InvoiceStatus
InvoiceStatus.description: An invoice's life. Nothing becomes a cost without a human passing through NEEDS_REVIEW.

InvoiceUpdate.title: InvoiceUpdate
InvoiceUpdate.description:
What the reader took from the invoice's header, corrected by the person looking at the PDF: a
date or a file reference read as the invoice's number, a forwarder not recognised. The number and
the forwarder are what every guard against counting an invoice twice compares, so a wrong one is
either a false refusal or a missed double entry. Only while the invoice is being reviewed; a field
left out is left as it is, and an empty one is cleared.

LandedCostReport.title: LandedCostReport
LandedCostReport.description:
Landed-cost figures only: recoverable import VAT is in `totals.vat` and in no other total.

The keys of `totals` are meant to be added up by the person reading them:
`allocated == estimated + actual`, `actual == matched_actual + unforecast_actual`, and
`variance == matched_actual - matched_estimated` on the `matched_pairs` estimates an invoice has
actually replaced. Nothing else compares an estimate with an invoice that was never its own.

MilestoneCode.title: MilestoneCode
MilestoneCode.description:
Tracking timeline vocabulary: every milestone a provider can report.

A superset of `ContainerMilestone` (the coarser state carried on the container itself); the extra
codes — empty pickup at origin, transshipment and rail legs, `UNKNOWN` — stay in the timeline.

PeriodAccrual.title: PeriodAccrual
PeriodAccrual.description:
Received and not yet invoiced at the end of the month: an estimate no invoice has replaced, on a
container that had landed by the last day of the month. *Factures non parvenues*, per cost type.

PeriodReadiness.title: PeriodReadiness
PeriodReadiness.description: What is better settled before closing. Never a refusal.

PreparationExample.title: PreparationExample
PreparationExample.description:
Something to click on: `kind` says which page, `id` which one — a uuid, or for a `sku` the
article code itself.

PreparationItem.title: PreparationItem
PreparationItem.description:
One thing that would make the audit wrong (`blocking`) or that it will not be able to say
(`limits`), counted, with the section it touches and a few examples. Codes and raw values: the
sentence and the remedy are the screen's. `params`: COSTS_UNALLOCATED `reason` (an engine code),
DUTY_GAP `pct` (the guard, "20"); none elsewhere.

PurchaseOrderStatus.title: PurchaseOrderStatus
PurchaseOrderStatus.description: Open, or cancelled upstream. Cancelling never deletes: the order may already carry costs.

RateBasis.title: RateBasis
RateBasis.description: How a rate card turns into an amount. What the forwarder's price list actually says.

ReportNote.title: ReportNote
ReportNote.description:
A rule applied to a cost that *was* allocated — never an amount missing from the total.

Same shape as a warning minus the amount, precisely so it cannot be rendered as "x € unallocated".

SampleDataDeleted.title: SampleDataDeleted
SampleDataDeleted.description: What DELETE /organization/sample-data took away, by kind.

SharedReportPublic.title: SharedReportPublic
SharedReportPublic.description: What a link opens: the report as it stood when the link was made, and nothing else.

SkuBox.title: SkuBox
SkuBox.description:
The article in one container, whatever number of order lines carried it there. This is what
`last_unit_landed`, `previous_unit_landed` and `change_pct` compare, and what a curve plots.

TrackingEventCreate.title: TrackingEventCreate
TrackingEventCreate.description: A milestone typed in by hand. `occurred_at` is when it happened, not when it was entered.

TrackingSubscriptionCreate.title: TrackingSubscriptionCreate
TrackingSubscriptionCreate.description:
`provider_ref` is the provider's own handle for this box. Leave it out when the provider is
subscribed through its API; give it when deliveries arrive webhook-only (no API key).

VarianceReport.title: VarianceReport
VarianceReport.description:
What the month's invoices cost against what was expected of them.

Only costs that replaced an estimate appear: an invoice nobody forecast has nothing to differ
from, and counting it as a 100 % overrun would be a lie by arithmetic.

WebhookAck.title: WebhookAck
WebhookAck.description:
What a provider gets back. Always 200 once the delivery is stored; `status` says what we did
with it, and a provider must not retry on `duplicate` or `failed`.
